title: Sri Lanka’s apex bench began hearing dozens of challenges to the proposal to raise judges’ retirement ages and expand the appeals cadre.
body_paragraphs: The sitting ran late into the night on the first day, then resumed the next morning before a five-judge panel. The state side argued the measure did not trigger a plebiscite under entrenched provisions, while opponents pressed that it touched people’s sovereignty and required both a supermajority and a popular vote.

Bar leaders later declined to file post‑hearing briefs after being denied an oral reply, and protesters rallied near Fort station. A determination will be sent to the Speaker within three weeks, even as street politics and courtroom manoeuvres converged around whether institutional efficiency can be advanced without eroding independence.

title: A catastrophic Himalayan flood left more than 900 dead and thousands missing, with Colombo pledging US$1 million and preparing relief teams.
body_paragraphs: The torrent, unleashed after a glacial collapse sent debris surging down transboundary mountain rivers, severed roads, damaged hydropower tunnels and destroyed crossings along a key border corridor. Officials in Kathmandu reported over 4,200 unaccounted for, while Beijing listed hundreds more, including foreign nationals.

Authorities in Sri Lanka said deployments would be finalised within days as alerts continued over a second barrier lake threatening breach upstream. The episode underscored accelerating high‑mountain hazard chains and the need for rapid early‑warning and cross‑border data sharing.

title: The merchandise trade gap widened by nearly 69% to US$6.51bn in the first seven months of 2026.
body_paragraphs: Imports climbed 25.8% year‑on‑year to US$14.64bn from January to July, led by a 59.9% fuel bill and the resumption of vehicle shipments that reached US$1.50bn. Exports rose only 4.4% to US$8.14bn as July receipts fell 5.3%, deepening monthly shortfalls.

The external current account slipped into a US$142m deficit in July, the fourth straight month in the red, even as remittances for the period grew 21.4% to US$5.38bn. Tourism earnings softened and overseas travel outlays jumped 72.7%, while terms of trade deteriorated as import prices outpaced export prices.

title: Headline inflation accelerated to 8.0% in August, breaching the upper edge of the target band.
body_paragraphs: Food prices quickened to 8.5% on the month, with higher costs for milk powder, dried fish, fresh fruit and green chillies outweighing declines in vegetables and sea fish. Non‑food rose 7.7%, with transport remaining the single largest annual contributor despite a modest cut to pump prices late in the month.

The monthly change was contained at 0.28% as adjustments to auto fuel and cooking gas aided the index. With the policy anchor set at 5% plus or minus two points, the tolerance will be judged on a quarterly average, leaving room for a glide back if supply‑side pressures ease.

title: Customs surpassed its August revenue goal ahead of month‑end, topping Rs.199.6bn by the 27th.
body_paragraphs: The collection put the agency over its monthly target of Rs.190.27bn with several days to spare, lifting the January‑August tally to roughly Rs.1.83trn against a full‑year aim of Rs.2.21trn. Officials expect the final August outturn to clear Rs.200bn once end‑month entries are posted.

title: World cricket moved the 2027 Women’s Champions Trophy to India, costing Sri Lanka a projected US$20m in host benefits.
body_paragraphs: The shift followed governance concerns over the local board’s transition process, with the event now slated for Mumbai and Vadodara in mid‑February under a six‑team T20I format. The national side retained automatic qualification on ranking, but the loss of staging rights dented expected tourism and operational income.

title: A US$12.5m smart‑meter rollout won approval to fit 300,000 connections with time‑of‑use billing.
body_paragraphs: The two‑year deployment, funded from an existing multilateral line, will be executed by the unbundled distribution entity as part of a wider grid‑modernisation core. The programme is intended to shift discretionary demand away from peak hours and cut losses by enabling granular pricing and remote measurement.

title: Electric commuter services were slated for three corridors radiating from the capital, with works to start by mid‑2027 and first phase due by 2030.
body_paragraphs: Plans cover the main line to Ragama, the coastal tracks to Panadura and the Kelani Valley route to Makumbura, alongside upgraded stations and new passenger amenities. Officials said the move targets faster, lower‑emission urban travel and is tied to a broader transport‑sector overhaul.

title: Equities snapped a three‑month slide in August even as year‑to‑date returns stayed negative.
body_paragraphs: The ASPI rose 0.99% for the month and the S&P SL20 added 1.17%, trimming part of July’s losses, while cumulative moves sat at minus 5.68% and minus 2.4% respectively. Turnover averaged Rs.3.64bn in August, with foreign participation muted and breadth mixed across sessions.

title: Colombo cleared a bilateral pact with Beijing to deepen immigration coordination and traveller facilitation.
body_paragraphs: The framework covers information exchange, official visits by agency heads and joint training to improve border‑management skills. It aims to smooth business, investment and tourism movements while supporting action against organised smuggling and trafficking, with authorities stressing it was unrelated to recent criminal arrests.
